QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_3

question.text: Jeevan Jyoti Foundation has raised Rs. 6 crore via a Zero-Coupon Zero-Principal (ZCZP) bond on BSE-SSE to fund a tele-medicine programme. The SIA is drafting the Annual Impact Report. Under SAS-100, which element is the MINIMUM mandatory content in Section I (Context) of the Report?

answer.text: Detailed donor-wise ZCZP subscription list with PAN and amount
About the project, responsibilities of the Reporting Entity and the SIA, and confirmation of the SAS standards applied
The SIA's audit fee, partner rotation cycle and firm peer-review status
The complete list of 16 eligible activities under SEBI ICDR Regulation 292B with the SE's chosen activity highlighted

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8's sample Social Impact Assessment Report (Swagruha example) shows Section I must cover: (i) about the project, (ii) responsibilities of reporting entity and social impact assessor, and (iii) confirmation of the SAS standards applied — the exact triad in Option B. The Trap: Option A violates donor confidentiality (PAN is personal data). Option C is engagement-admin, not a Context disclosure. Option D pads the Report with regulation that's already public. Cross-Exam Context: Analogous to the scope/purpose/responsibilities triad in assurance reports discussed in V-A (MF Distributor — disclosure) and III-A / III-C (Compliance). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Draft Section I last, not first — once you have finalised scope boundaries (geography, period, activity), the Context paragraph almost writes itself from the engagement letter.
